questions.statement: In the context of ai & future of work, which word best completes the following sentence: 'The government's failure to address the issue has only served to __________ the social divide'?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Medellín.

options.text: exacerbate
options.feedback: Correct. 'Exacerbate' means to make a problem or bad situation worse, which fits perfectly here.

options.text: alleviate
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Alleviate' means to make something less severe, which is the opposite of what's needed.

options.text: mitigate
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Mitigate' means to make something less severe, which doesn't fit the negative consequence implied.

options.text: facilitate
options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Facilitate' means to make an action or process easy or easier, which is not appropriate for a social divide.

questions.explanation:
This question tests advanced vocabulary (verbs of change and impact) suitable for C1+ level.

questions.statement: In the context of ai & future of work, which word best completes the following sentence: 'A hiring model deployed without an audit of its training data can __________ candidates from groups the data never represented'?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Pereira.

options.text: exclude
options.feedback: 'Exclude' means to leave out or bar from participation, and the sentence describes a screening model that filters out people who never appeared in its training set.

options.text: exploit
options.feedback: 'Exploit' means to use unfairly or take advantage of, and the clause is about candidates being left out rather than being used.

options.text: expose
options.feedback: 'Expose' means to make something visible or vulnerable, and the sentence is about exclusion from a process, not about disclosure.

options.text: excuse
options.feedback: 'Excuse' means to forgive or justify, and nothing in the clause describes absolution or a reason offered for someone's conduct.

questions.explanation:
The preposition 'from' marks what is left out, and 'exclude' is the verb that carries that sense: the model bars candidates whose groups were absent from its training data. The other options all concern using, revealing or forgiving, and none of them fits a filter that removes applicants.

questions.statement: In the context of ai & future of work, which word best completes the following sentence: 'The promise that automation would shorten the working week has so far __________ the hours of the people it was meant to liberate'?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Manizales.

options.text: extended
options.feedback: 'Extend' means to make something longer in time or space, and the sentence reports the opposite of the promised effect: the working day grew instead of shrinking.

options.text: intended
options.feedback: 'Intend' means to plan or mean to do something, and the clause reports a measurable outcome rather than an intention held by the proponents.

options.text: attended
options.feedback: 'Attend' means to be present at, and the sentence is about the length of a working week rather than anyone's presence at an event.

options.text: invented
options.feedback: 'Invent' means to create something new, and the clause says a promise had an effect on hours, which is a claim about duration rather than about origin.

questions.explanation:
The concessive structure 'has so far' signals that the expected benefit failed to appear, and the verb has to name what actually happened to the hours: they became longer. 'Extended' captures that reversal, while the other options describe intention, presence or invention, none of which the clause supports.

questions.statement: A manager says, 'I concede that the AI system still makes errors.' What does 'concede' mean in this statement?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Pereira.

options.text: To predict that something will happen.
options.feedback: Predict refers to forecasting an event; the manager is acknowledging an existing limitation.

options.text: To order someone to change something.
options.feedback: Order expresses a command, but the manager is admitting a point rather than directing an action.

options.text: To admit a point, often reluctantly.
options.feedback: Concede means to acknowledge that a point is true, often when it weakens one's position in a discussion.

options.text: To reject a claim as false.
options.feedback: Rejecting a claim would mean denying the errors, whereas concede acknowledges that the system makes them.

questions.explanation: Concede is a reporting verb used to acknowledge a point, often reluctantly. Here, the manager admits a limitation of the AI system.

questions.statement: An analyst says to the company, 'You should retrain employees before introducing the AI tool.' Which reported version preserves this advice and uses the correct verb pattern?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Pereira.

options.text: The analyst recommended to retrain employees before introducing the AI tool.
options.feedback: Recommend does not normally take a direct to-infinitive complement; recommended retraining is the appropriate pattern here.

options.text: The analyst denied retraining employees before introducing the AI tool.
options.feedback: Denied retraining rejects a claim about an action; it does not report advice that the company should retrain employees.

options.text: The analyst recommended retraining employees before introducing the AI tool.
options.feedback: Recommend can be followed by an -ing form, and retraining accurately reports the proposed action as advice.

options.text: The analyst promised to retrain employees before introducing the AI tool.
options.feedback: Promised to retrain makes the analyst commit to performing the training, which changes advice into a personal commitment.

questions.explanation: Recommend plus an -ing form reports a suggested course of action. It preserves the analyst's advice without making the analyst responsible for carrying it out.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: A supervisor tells the staff, 'Do not upload customers' private records to the public chatbot.' Which sentence accurately reports this warning?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Pereira.

options.text: The supervisor encouraged the staff to upload customers' private records to the public chatbot.
options.feedback: Encouraged reverses the message by promoting the action that the supervisor explicitly prohibited.

options.text: The supervisor warned the staff not to upload customers' private records to the public chatbot.
options.feedback: Warned the staff not to upload uses warn plus an object and a negative to-infinitive to preserve the caution against uploading.

options.text: The supervisor admitted uploading customers' private records to the public chatbot.
options.feedback: Admitted uploading describes the supervisor acknowledging a personal action, not warning the staff against it.

options.text: The supervisor offered to upload customers' private records to the public chatbot.
options.feedback: Offered to upload presents a voluntary action by the supervisor, which contradicts the instruction not to upload.

questions.explanation: Warn someone not to do something reports a caution against an action. The object identifies the people receiving the warning, and the negative infinitive preserves the prohibition.

options.text: had

questions.statement: A fictional news report states: 'The software vendor claimed that its hiring algorithm was unbiased, but the independent audit had not yet been completed.' Why is 'claimed' more appropriate than 'confirmed'?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Bucaramanga.

options.text: Claimed proves that the algorithm was biased.
options.feedback: Claimed marks an assertion without establishing its truth; it does not prove the opposite assertion that the algorithm was biased.

options.text: Claimed indicates that the vendor asked the auditors a question.
options.feedback: Claimed reports an assertion, whereas asked would report a question or request.

options.text: Claimed means that the audit had already verified the vendor's statement.
options.feedback: The report explicitly says the audit was incomplete, so the wording cannot mean that independent verification had already occurred.

options.text: Claimed attributes the assertion to the vendor without presenting it as an established finding.
options.feedback: Claimed maintains a distinction between the vendor's assertion and verified evidence; confirmed would suggest that the assertion had been established.

questions.explanation: Reporting verbs communicate the evidential status of a statement. Claimed attributes an unverified assertion to its source, while confirmed would imply verification that the report does not provide.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the following sentence about ai & future of work: 'Scarcely __________ the model finished retraining on local data than its accuracy fell apart in rural areas.' (Topic: inversion with 'scarcely ... than')
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Manizales.

options.text: has
options.feedback: 'Has' would give the present perfect, but the clause reports a past completed action followed immediately by a past consequence, which requires the past perfect.

options.text: had
options.feedback: 'Scarcely had the model finished retraining than its accuracy fell apart'. The past perfect fixes the completed action that 'scarcely' denies as having fully happened.

options.text: did
options.feedback: 'Did' would invert a simple past, but the participle 'finished' requires an auxiliary of perfect aspect rather than the do-form of inversion.

options.text: was
options.feedback: 'Was' cannot invert before a past participle; the passive form would also contradict the active training described in the clause.

questions.explanation:
'Scarcely ... than' fixes the first event as complete before the second arrives, which is exactly what the past perfect expresses. The auxiliary 'had' precedes the subject and the participle 'finished' carries the tense, so the sequence is 'had the model finished'. Present perfect forms are the usual error because they place the action too close to the consequence.

questions.statement: Complete the following sentence about ai & future of work: 'Under no circumstances __________ automated scoring replace a decision that the public is entitled to contest.' (Topic: inversion with a negative adverbial and a modal verb)
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Pereira.

options.text: must
options.feedback: 'Must' is a modal, but the blank needs the inverted auxiliary that 'under no circumstances' requires, and a modal cannot follow the adverbial in a declarative inversion of this kind without another element.

options.text: should
options.feedback: 'Under no circumstances should automated scoring replace'. A modal inverts exactly as the auxiliary of an ordinary verb does, so fronting 'should' produces the emphatic reading.

options.text: would
options.feedback: 'Would' belongs to the conditional or the reporting sequence here, not to the emphatic inversion the negative adverbial demands.

options.text: ought
options.feedback: 'Ought' takes 'to' plus an infinitive, so it could not fill the gap directly after the negative adverbial in this construction.

questions.explanation:
Negative adverbials such as 'under no circumstances', 'in no way' and 'not at all' trigger inversion of the first auxiliary, and modals invert in exactly the same way. Fronting 'should' ahead of the subject 'automated scoring' produces the emphatic reading. A modal of obligation or conditional aspect does not carry the contrastive force of 'should' in this negated frame.

questions.statement: Complete the following sentence about ai & future of work: 'No sooner __________ the pilot go live than complaints about biased shortlists began to arrive.' (Topic: 'no sooner ... than' inversion)
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Barranquilla.

options.text: did
options.feedback: 'Did' with a bare infinitive would need 'no sooner had'; the participle 'gone' shows that the perfect auxiliary is required rather than the do-form.

options.text: had
options.feedback: 'No sooner had the pilot gone live than complaints arrived'. The structure pairs a completed past action with the immediate consequence that followed it.

options.text: has
options.feedback: 'Has' would give the present perfect and place the action in unfinished time, whereas 'no sooner ... than' needs a bounded past sequence.

options.text: was
options.feedback: 'Was' cannot combine with a past participle in this active construction, and the clause clearly states that the pilot launched it.

questions.explanation:
The correlative pair 'no sooner ... than' obliges the perfect auxiliary before the participle, so the first clause reads 'had the pilot gone live'. The second clause then arrives with 'than', marking the consequence that followed immediately. Choosing a present perfect or a simple do-inversion breaks the bounded past sequence the pattern requires.

questions.statement: Complete the following sentence about ai & future of work: 'Seldom __________ a retraining programme survive the change of minister who commissioned it.' (Topic: inversion with 'seldom' and a singular subject)
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Medellín.

options.text: do
options.feedback: 'Do' agrees with plural subjects, and 'a retraining programme' is singular, so the base form with 'does' is the correct inversion.

options.text: have
options.feedback: 'Have' would give the perfect aspect, but the bare inversion with 'seldom' and a singular subject requires 'does' before the base form.

options.text: are
options.feedback: 'Are' would be needed for a plural subject. 'A programme' is singular, and 'seldom' does not alter the agreement of the auxiliary.

options.text: does
options.feedback: 'Seldom does a programme survive'. The singular subject takes 'does' and the main verb reverts to the base form 'survive'.

questions.explanation:
The singular subject 'a retraining programme' determines the auxiliary: after 'seldom' it inverts as 'does', and the verb 'survive' loses its third person ending. Because 'do' is much more frequent with plural subjects in this structure, students often carry that agreement across, which is precisely the error this item tests.

questions.statement: In a high-level debate about ai & future of work, Daniela says: 'I can't help but feel that we are barking up the wrong tree with this approach.' What does Daniela mean?
questions.context: Discussing ai & future of work in Pereira.

options.text: The current strategy is directed towards the wrong objective.
options.feedback: Correct. This idiom means to follow a wrong line of thought or course of action.

options.text: They are literally looking for something in the trees of {city}.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is a literal and incorrect interpretation of the idiom.

options.text: The approach is too noisy and aggressive.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The idiom relates to direction/objective, not volume or attitude.

options.text: A new environmental project involving trees should be started.
options.feedback: Incorrect. This misinterprets the figurative meaning of the phrase.

questions.explanation:
Pragmatic competence at C1+ involves understanding and using idiomatic expressions in formal contexts.
